text: CHAPTER 35
speaker: Narrator

text: The Lie He Told
speaker: Narrator
note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

text: Ninsun caught up within a dozen paces.
speaker: Narrator

text: She did not run and she did not shout. She simply walked alongside him, her presence a weight he had not asked for and could not put down.
speaker: Narrator

text: The corridor stretched ahead, narrow and oppressive. Torchlight died against the darkness before it could reach the walls.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik kept his eyes fixed forward.
speaker: Narrator

text: You lied,
speaker: Ninsun

text: Ninsun said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Her voice contained no anger. That was worse. It was flat and clinical, the voice of someone examining a wound and deciding, with professional detachment, how deep it went and whether it would scar.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik kept walking.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: I haven't said anything.
speaker: Zik

text: You read the journal. You closed it. You decided what the rest of us were allowed to know.
speaker: Ninsun

text: She placed each word carefully.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: That is a lie of a different kind. You have never once refused to show me the words before.
speaker: Ninsun

text: He stopped.
speaker: Narrator

text: The journal was warm against his fingers when he pulled it free. The mark under the linen on his palm pulsed once, slow and deliberate, as if the account were taking notice of the intention itself.
speaker: Narrator

text: He intended to open it. He intended to end the accusation with evidence.
speaker: Narrator

text: He did not open it.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun watched the decision form on his face.
speaker: Narrator

text: You're still deciding,
speaker: Ninsun

text: she said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Even now.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Balag's voice carried from ahead.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: If the two of you are going to stand there arguing about paper, the rest of us are moving.
speaker: Balag

text: Enhedu did not look back. She simply continued walking, the figurine turning once in her hand and then forgotten again.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik returned the journal to the satchel. The weight of the decision settled differently this time—not the clean absence of a payment already made, but the heavier, unfinished pressure of a payment deferred.
speaker: Narrator

text: They walked in silence until the corridor forked.
speaker: Narrator

text: Three identical passages opened ahead, each sloping downward at the same angle, each breathing with the same slow rhythm. The torchlight revealed nothing that distinguished one from the others.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun stepped forward and studied the stone above each opening. When she began to copy one of the incomplete symbols, the mark on her parchment went blank under the stylus.
speaker: Narrator

text: They're the same,
speaker: Ninsun

text: she said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Or the City wants us to believe they're the same.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Enhedu looked at the three openings with the remote attention she now gave anything that could not be priced.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Then we pick one and stop standing here.
speaker: Enhedu
note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

text: Balag shook his head.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Last time we picked, the walls rearranged themselves behind us. I'd rather know which one is the trap.
speaker: Balag

text: They're all traps,
speaker: Ninsun

text: Ninsun said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: The only question is which trap the City prefers us to choose.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Zik opened the journal.
speaker: Narrator

text: The page that had been blank a moment earlier now held a single line in the hand that was neither his father's nor his own:
speaker: Narrator

text: THE LEFT PATH BELONGS TO THE ONE WHO WAS NEVER SENT.
speaker: Narrator
note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

text: He read it twice. The sentence did not say the path was safe. It did not say the path was dangerous. It only assigned ownership.
speaker: Narrator

text: He closed the book before anyone else could see it.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun was watching his face.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: What does it say?
speaker: Ninsun

text: He could have told her. He could have shown her the page. He could have treated the information as shared rather than private.
speaker: Narrator

text: He looked at the three openings, at Balag waiting for direction, at Enhedu already half-turned toward the left-hand passage because someone else would eventually declare one of them relevant.
speaker: Narrator

text: He converted ownership into safety because safety was the word that would make the others follow.
speaker: Narrator
